title: D-003: .writing-framework/ as Central Portable Folder
body:
# D-003: .writing-framework/ as Central Portable Folder

**Date:** 2026-03-28
**Status:** Active

## Decision

All canonical framework content lives in `.writing-framework/` — doctrine, commands, agents, styles, workflows, schemas, guides, templates, examples. This folder is the unit of export and import between repos.

## Why

The framework must be portable. When installing this framework in a new repo, you copy `.writing-framework/`. When syncing a framework update, you compare `.writing-framework/` against the source. Having a single well-named root folder makes the portability boundary explicit and unambiguous.

Portability requires a single, identifiable unit. If framework content is distributed across multiple root-level directories (doctrine/, styles/, agents/ etc.), the install process must track and synchronize each directory independently, increasing the risk of missing a component during installation or sync. A single `.writing-framework/` folder is a single unit: copy it, sync it, version it.

## Original Design

`core/` was used initially. Renamed to `.writing-framework/` to use the hidden-folder convention (like `.git/`, `.github/`, `.claude/`) and give it a meaningful name. The hidden-folder convention signals to humans that this is infrastructure, not project content — it will not appear in standard directory listings and will not be confused with the project's own deliverables.

## Alternatives Considered

**Keep content at repo root** (doctrine/, styles/, etc.). Rejected: no clear portability boundary, tool adapters cannot reference a single folder.

**Name it `framework/`.** Rejected: not hidden, could conflict with project content in repos that already have a framework/ directory.

**Name it `.editorial/`.** Considered valid. `.writing-framework/` chosen for specificity — the name communicates the folder's purpose to someone encountering it for the first time.

## Consequences

All tool adapters reference `.writing-framework/` as the canonical source. Sync operations target `.writing-framework/`. Paths in CLAUDE.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and README.md all use `.writing-framework/` prefix. Agents and commands that reference content outside `.writing-framework/` (e.g., from `artifacts/` or `logs/`) must handle those as repo-specific content, not as framework content subject to sync.
